newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rules in favor of Union Pacific unit.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rules in favor of Union Pacific unit.

text.p: U.S. regulators have ruled that the flat rate charged by Missouri Pacific Railroad Co., part of Union Pacific Corp., to move South-West Railroad Car Parts Co. retired cars was not unreasonable.

South-West had challeged the reasonableness of a $300 per car rate levied over a two-and-one-half year period for moving old cars on their own wheels from five points in Texas and Louisiana to the firm's salvage yard in Greggton, Texas.

The Surface Transportation Board said in its preliminary decision this week that the rate was not out of line with the carrier's revenue requirements and the South-West traffic did not receive a disproportionately high price markup for traffic of its type.
But the board gave South-West until March 3 to introduce further evidence or arguments to back its case.
